html:
The Senas were a Hindu dynasty that ruled Bengal from the late 11th to the early 13th century. On this map they appear in 1000 and 1100, drawn over eastern Bengal and the hills beyond it, though their power really grew in the later 11th century.

Their family came from the south, from Karnataka, and served the Buddhist Pala Empire. As the Palas weakened, Vijayasena made himself master of Bengal. His son Ballala Sena and grandson Lakshmana Sena ruled a realm that backed Brahmin Hinduism, and Sanskrit poetry flourished; the Gita Govinda was written by Jayadeva, said to be a poet at Lakshmana Sena's court.

Around 1204 the Turkish commander Bakhtiyar Khalji raided Nadia, and Lakshmana Sena fled east. Western Bengal passed under Muslim rule, later part of the Delhi Sultanate. Sena kings held on in eastern Bengal for a few more decades.
